title: Past Tense and Aspect
intro: In past tense, aspect choice becomes crucial. Both 'Я читал книгу' and 'Я прочитал книгу' are past tense, but they mean different things! Imperfective past describes WHAT you were doing (process, duration). Perfective past describes WHAT you accomplished (result, completion). Context clues like 'долго' (long time) or 'наконец' (finally) often signal which aspect to use.
rules: Imperfective past = was doing, used to do, did repeatedly: Я читал книгу (I was reading).
Perfective past = did and finished, accomplished: Я прочитал книгу (I finished reading).
Duration/frequency words → imperfective: долго, часто, весь день, каждый день.
Result/completion words → perfective: уже, наконец, за час (in an hour), вдруг (suddenly).
examples: Что ты делал вчера? — Я читал книгу. (What did you do? — I was reading a book.), process
Ты прочитал книгу? — Да, прочитал. (Did you finish the book? — Yes, I did.), result
Я долго писал письмо. (I wrote the letter for a long time.), duration = imperfective
Я написал письмо за час. (I wrote the letter in an hour.), completion time = perfective

items.prompt: Что ты _____ вчера вечером? (What were you doing yesterday evening?)
items.promptEnglish: What were you doing yesterday evening?
items.explanation: 'What were you doing?' asks about process → imperfective.

items.prompt: Я уже _____ домашнее задание. (I already finished my homework.)
Она весь день _____ на работе. (She worked all day.)
Он наконец _____ эту задачу! (He finally solved this problem!)
Мы часто _____ в этом ресторане. (We often ate at this restaurant.)
items.promptEnglish: We often ate at this restaurant.

items.prompt: Я _____ письмо за пять минут. (I wrote the letter in five minutes.)
items.promptEnglish: I wrote the letter in five minutes.
items.hint: За + time = how long it took to complete = perfective

items.prompt: Когда я _____, вдруг зазвонил телефон. (While I was reading, suddenly the phone rang.)
items.promptEnglish: While I was reading, suddenly the phone rang.
items.hint: Background action (when something else happened) = imperfective

items.prompt: Он _____ и ушёл. (He ate and left.)
items.explanation: Both actions completed in sequence → perfective.

items.prompt: Раньше я каждый день _____ газету. (I used to read the newspaper every day.)
items.promptEnglish: I used to read the newspaper every day.

items.prompt: Change to past tense (male speaker), emphasizing the process of reading: Я читаю книгу.
items.explanation: An ongoing process uses the imperfective past: читаю → читал.

items.prompt: Change to past tense (male speaker), emphasizing you finished reading: Я читаю книгу.
items.explanation: A completed action uses the perfective past: читаю → прочитал.

items.prompt: Change to past tense, emphasizing she finished: Она делает уроки.
items.explanation: A completed action uses the perfective past: делает → сделала.

blanks: Вчера мы _____ новый фильм, а потом пошли в кафе. (Yesterday we watched a new movie and then went to a café.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Watching a movie to completion = perfective
hints: Watching a movie from start to finish implies a completed action. Which aspect signals completion in the past?
explanations: Watching a movie to the end is a completed, one-time action, so use perfective past: посмотрели (watched fully), not смотрели (were watching).

minimalPairs.context: Я два часа _____ письмо. (I wrote/was writing the letter for two hours.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I was writing the letter for two hours.

minimalPairs.context: Я _____ письмо и отправил его. (I wrote the letter and sent it.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I wrote the letter and sent it.
minimalPairs.explanation: Completed action, then next action → perfective: написал.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort signal words: imperfective or perfective?

reviewVocab.definition: for a long time / in (amount of) time
reviewVocab.example: Долго писал (was writing). Написал за час (wrote in an hour).
